clue.text: Pot manufactured for ointment

parts.note: a po is a chamber pot
manufactured means made

explanation.surface: A pot has been produced for holding some ointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot manufactured' looks like an anagram, but PO is the chamber pot and MADE stands for manufactured.
explanation.definitionFit: A scented hair ointment, once widely used by men, is a classic example of this greasy preparation.

clue.text: Publicist wants sales-people brought up to succeed

parts.note: a PRO is a public relations officer, a publicist

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the word is written upwards

parts.note: reps are sales representatives

explanation.surface: A publicist wants the sales team promoted to help them succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to do well and flourish, which is to succeed.

clue.text: Two males engaging a very sucessful lawyer

indicators.note: engaging means the two male pieces hold the article between them

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male; a son is another male
a son is a male, the second of the pair

explanation.surface: Two men hire a top-notch attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: Perry Mason, the TV and fiction lawyer, almost never lost a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Perry Mason is the fictional defence attorney famed for winning nearly every case.

clue.text: Security bound to be on the rise outside post offices

indicators.note: outside means the turned word wraps round the postal abbreviation
on the rise in a down clue means the word is written upwards

parts.note: bound means tied
PO is the abbreviation for post office, so POs for more than one

explanation.surface: Security is sure to be rising around post offices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rise' turns TIED into DEIT, which goes outside POS.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is money given as security, as on a rented flat.

clue.text: Long distance makes one break down, literally, and start to cry

parts.note: to parse a sentence is to break it down into its grammatical parts, i.e. to break it down by its letters and words

indicators.note: the start of the word cry gives just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Something makes a person collapse and begin to weep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break down' suggests collapsing in tears; here it is the grammarian's analysis of a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomical unit of length of about 3.26 light years, so a very long distance indeed.

clue.text: A holy woman not married buzzes around here?

parts.note: pi is informal for pious, holy

indicators.note: not means the marriage abbreviation is taken out

parts.note: Mary is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A pious unmarried woman wonders whether people gossip about her here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buzzes around here' looks like gossip; it is bees buzzing round their hives.
explanation.definitionFit: An apiary is a place where beehives are kept, so where bees buzz about.

clue.text: Ecstacy lacking in the mission that spreads religion

indicators.note: lacking says the drug letter is missing from the letter pool
spreads says the remaining letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for the letter pool
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A mission without drugs spreads its faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E from THE MISSION and rearrange THMISSION.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the native religion of Japan, and this is its name as an -ism.

clue.text: Roughly, a source of smoke that comes with the end of battle time?

definitions.text: Roughly, a source of smoke that comes with the end of battle time?

parts.note: ca, for circa, means roughly
a lum is a chimney in Scots dialect

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word battle

explanation.surface: A rough guess at what gives off smoke at the close of a war.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the pipe of peace was smoked when fighting ended.
explanation.definitionFit: A calumet is a Native American ceremonial pipe, smoked as a pledge of peace after conflict.

clue.text: Musicians — six going for a walk — they go up and down

indicators.note: going for means the numeral is replaced by the walk

parts.note: violinists are musicians
VI is the Roman numeral for six
a tramp is a long walk

explanation.surface: Some musicians, six of them, head out on a hike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they go up and down' sounds like hikers on hills, but describes bouncers.
explanation.definitionFit: Trampoline performers bounce repeatedly upwards and downwards.

clue.text: One who wrote about blondes being mostly promiscuous

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter, leaving most of it

parts.note: loose, in its old-fashioned sense, means promiscuous

explanation.surface: A writer on blondes is accused of being rather promiscuous.
explanation.walkthrough: Anita Loos wrote Gentlemen Prefer Blondes.
explanation.definitionFit: Anita Loos was the American author of the novel Gentlemen Prefer Blondes.

clue.text: Form of verb giving power to one page in Guardian piece?

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics

indicators.note: in places the one-and-page pair inside the newspaper piece

parts.note: an article is a piece in a newspaper such as the Guardian
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A grammar question about strengthening a verb form in a newspaper column.
explanation.definitionFit: A participle, such as running or broken, is a verbal form used as an adjective or in compound tenses.

clue.text: What minister (slimy MP?) does if he goes off?

definitions.text: What minister (slimy MP?) does if he goes off?

parts.words: What minister (slimy MP?) does if he goes off?
parts.note: the stock excuse a disgraced government minister gives on resigning, claiming he wants to be at home with his wife and children

explanation.surface: A politician quits under a cloud and offers the usual excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes off' means resigns, though it hints at going rotten, matching 'slimy'.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase is the familiar euphemism British politicians use when resigning after a scandal.

clue.text: Time of trial for cricketer at the wicket collecting duck

parts.note: pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons
a bat is a batsman in cricket

indicators.note: collecting means the batting word takes the zero-score letter inside it

parts.note: a cricket batsman at the wicket is in
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A batsman on trial at the crease scores nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman currently batting is 'in'; a duck is a score of zero, shaped like an O.
explanation.definitionFit: Probation is a trial period, for a new employee or an offender under supervision.

clue.text: Auntie Deb's silly gas

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters are jumbled foolishly

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Auntie Deb talks a lot of hot air.
explanation.definitionFit: Butadiene is a hydrocarbon gas used to make synthetic rubber.

clue.text: Border's catalogue

definitions.meaning: a strip or selvage on the edge of cloth, so a border
a catalogue is an itemised record of things

explanation.definitionFit: Both an archaic edging strip of cloth and an itemised register share this short word.

clue.text: See 11
Western countries united in battle not the wisest folk?

parts.note: allies are nations joined together in war

explanation.surface: Western nations fighting together are hardly the cleverest.
explanation.walkthrough: Wally is British slang for a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallies, British slang, are foolish or inept people.

clue.text: Journalist's wild about supporter of union

indicators.note: about means the wild word goes round the journalist

parts.note: feral means wild
ED, an editor, is a journalist; 's is no letter

explanation.surface: A journalist goes wild about a trade unionist.
explanation.definitionFit: A federalist backs a union of states, and the adjective describes that kind of union.

clue.text: Beatle hit? Ah, this could be it!

definitions.text: Beatle hit? Ah, this could be it!

parts.words: Beatle hit? Ah, this could be it!
parts.note: a 1970 Beatles single whose title is a phrase of acceptance; the solver hunting for a Beatles song is told the clue itself could be the answer

explanation.surface: A fan guessing at a Beatles single.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a 1970 Beatles single and album, and an idiom for leaving things alone.

clue.text: Actor's rude graffiti?

definitions.meaning: Humphrey, the Casablanca film star; 's stands for is
scrawlings on a toilet wall, bog being British slang for toilet

explanation.surface: An actor is accused of crude scrawls.
explanation.walkthrough: Bog is British slang for a toilet, so toilet-wall graffiti is bog art.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphrey Bogart was the American film star of Casablanca.

clue.text: Plants I record including one leguminous one bent back

indicators.note: bent back says the whole assembled string is read in the opposite direction
including puts the one-and-pulse pair inside the record word

parts.note: a log is a record
I is the Roman numeral for one
dal is a lentil or similar pulse, a leguminous plant

explanation.surface: A gardener records plants, one of them a bent-over legume.
explanation.walkthrough: Assembled forwards the pieces give ILOIDALG; 'bent back' turns this round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladioli are tall flowering garden plants with sword-shaped leaves.

clue.text: Party has crazy American food

parts.note: a do is a party
nuts means crazy

explanation.surface: A party serves wild American snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: This American spelling names ring-shaped fried dough cakes, a typical US snack.

clue.text: Wickedness upset Pasquale in that French city

indicators.note: in places the setter inside the turned word
upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: sin means wickedness
the setter refers to himself, so me

explanation.surface: Wickedness distresses the setter in a city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often use their own name for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Nîmes is a city in southern France known for its Roman remains.

clue.text: Bit of a drinker and good-for-nothing home movie captured

indicators.note: captured means the home-and-film pair are held inside the idler

parts.note: a waster is a good-for-nothing
in means at home
ET is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker and layabout is caught on home video.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of a drinker' is someone who drinks only a little, a sip at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional taster sips small amounts of wine, so is a drinker only in small bits.

clue.text: For American children a subject that's dull and hard?

parts.note: mat (matt) means dull, not glossy
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: American schoolchildren find a certain subject boring and difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans shorten mathematics to this form, where Britons say maths.

clue.text: Society man once in politics gets protection

parts.note: Edward Heath was a British Prime Minister in the 1970s

explanation.surface: A society figure who used to be a politician gets security.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath was Conservative Prime Minister of the UK from 1970 to 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a protective covering, as for a blade.

clue.text: Fabric that's soft is displayed in london School

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

indicators.note: displayed in puts the small word inside the college abbreviation

parts.note: LSE is the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: A soft material is exhibited at a London college.
explanation.definitionFit: Plissé is a cotton or other fabric with a puckered, pleated finish.
